subject: Outmarket AI
object: $34.5M Series B to Solidify Position as the #1 AI Platform for Insurance
source_quote: In conjunction with the Series B announcement, Outmarket released a new Certificates workflow. Certificates of insurance are one of the highest volume and most thankless tasks in every agency. Account managers issue thousands of certificates a year, often within hours of a client request, and every one carries E&O exposure if a holder, endorsement or coverage requirement is missed. Outmarket's Certificates workflow automates the entire process. It reads the client's contract or lease, extracts the insurance requirements, checks them against the policies already in the AMS, flags any gaps, and generates the completed ACORD certificate with the correct holders, additional insureds and endorsements attached. Early customers report issuing certificates in a few minutes and significantly reducing certificate-related errors.

subject: Volantis
object: $88 million for tech to connect AI, memory chips
source_quote: Nvidia and AMD solve the problem by encircling their computing chips with expensive high-bandwidth memory chips.San Francisco-based semiconductor startup Volantis on Thursday said it has raised $88 million in venture capital in an effort to solve a key challenge for AI chips by tapping a technology that is already sitting in hundreds of millions of iPhones.The fundamental limit for AI chips from both Nvidia and rivals like Advanced Micro Devices is how well the computing parts of a chip can talk to the memory chips where an AI model lives and feeds data to the computing chip. Nvidia and AMD solve the problem by encircling their computing chips with expensive high-bandwidth memory chips.But even Nvidia's best current offerings can hold only eight of those memory chips for each of its graphics processing units (GPUs) because of the limited reach of the tiny electrical wires that connect the memory chips. Volantis says it is developing a way to send data between computing chips and memory chips using beams of laser light, which eliminates the reach problem and would let it pack 220 memory chips around a GPU.To do that, Volantis is tapping what are called vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers, or VCSELs. While the tiny lasers sound exotic, they power the facial recognition features in many devices from Apple, which invested heavily in bolstering the supply chain over the past decade.By bringing together relatively well-known components, Volantis is hoping to avoid some of the supply chainbottlenecks in developing AI chips and deliver a chip next year that would speed up tasks like AI coding, said Tapa Ghosh, CEO and co-founder of Volantis, in an interview."Advanced packaging is always to be respected - it's never trivial - but it's not necessarily a new thing to do," Ghosh said. "No one is going to win a Nobel Prize if our project works, but the good news is, they won't need to."The funding round was led by Stripe veteran Lachy Groom and Abstract Ventures. John Doerr, who backed Google and Amazon.com in their early days, also participated, as did VXI Capital, Triatomic and Susa Ventures. The round also includes angel investments from AI podcaster Dwarkesh Patel, AI chip veteran Naveen Rao and Anthropic researcher Sholto Douglas.

subject: RapidAPI co-founder
object: $15 million for AI marketing startup enso
source_quote: Israeli startup enso, which develops AI agent systems for marketing and sales, has raised $15 million in a Series A round led by MoreTech Ventures, with participation from existing investor NFX, Phenomen VC, and Gil Hirsch. The round brings the company’s total funding to $23 million. Full list of Israeli high-tech funding rounds in 2026 The new capital will be used to expand enso’s operations in what the company calls “Agentic Growth Hacking,” as businesses increasingly rely on AI tools to reach customers. The way companies reach customers is changing rapidly. Search algorithms, social media feeds and AI answer engines increasingly determine which businesses and products users encounter. Consumers and businesses are also turning to tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews to research companies and products alongside traditional search engines and social networks. That creates a moving target for marketers. Strategies that work today can lose their effectiveness as platforms change their algorithms, recommendation systems and rules, while user behavior evolves. Enso’s AI agents analyze how different platforms rank, recommend and cite content. They then test different approaches through small-scale experiments and measure the results. When an approach proves effective, enso can turn it into a repeatable growth mechanism for a customer. Tactics that stop working can be retested or abandoned. The company currently works with enterprises and startups including Papaya Global, MyHeritage, Papaya Gaming, Natural Intelligence, Winn AI and Israel Canada. For each customer, enso embeds an engineer and a marketer who connect the research to the company’s existing sales and marketing operations, systems and brand. The team builds a set of agents around those workflows and measures their performance against an established business and pipeline baseline. The systems operate across several channels, including search and AI-answer visibility, sales outreach, online communities, newsletters and social media. In AI search, for example, enso tracks which companies and sources are cited in answers to relevant questions and measures whether changes in content and distribution affect a customer’s visibility. Human oversight remains part of the system. Marketers determine strategy, brand boundaries and which playbooks are deployed, while the agents handle ongoing monitoring, testing and execution. Sensitive or irreversible actions remain under human control. Enso was founded in 2024 by Mickey Haslavsky, who serves as CEO and previously co-founded RapidAPI. Haslavsky coined the term “Agentic Growth Hacking” and is writing a book under the same title. The company employs 26 people, most of them based in Israel. enso publishes research on its experiments, including unsuccessful ones and the lessons learned from them, and maintains open-source reference skills for AI agents. “Marketing teams can spend months building a strategy around channels that change before they see results,” Haslavsky said. “AI agents make it possible to monitor multiple platforms continuously, test where opportunities are emerging and act while those opportunities still matter. We embed an engineer and a marketer with the customer, build the system around how they operate, measure against a baseline and keep a person accountable for what the agents do.”

The company could debut as soon as October and raise up to $100 billion via the offering, according to a recent report in The Wall Street Journal, while OpenAI, which Reuters says filed confidentially in June, is reportedly now looking toward early 2027.

subject: Physical AI company SiMa.ai
object: $150 Mn in Series C round
source_quote: "Physical AI company SiMa.ai has raised $150 million in a Series C financing round, bringing its total capital raised to $500 million and valuing the company at $1.45 billion. The round was co-led by Fidelity Management &amp; Research Company and Amplify, with participation from Alter Venture Partners, Dell Technologies Capital and StepStone Group. AllianceBernstein, Baron Capital and J.P. Morgan also joined the round as new investors. The proceeds will be used to scale Palette Neat, an agentic software environment for Physical AI, and develop next-generation hardware capable of delivering 1,000 TOPS of compute through purpose-built Physical AI silicon, SiMa.ai said in a press release. Founded in 2018 by Krishna Rangasayee, SiMa.ai provides a software-centric platform for Physical AI applications. The company focuses on robotics, automotive, drones, industrial automation, aerospace and defence, smart vision and healthcare. SiMa.ai said it serves more than 150 customers across automotive, drones and robotics, including ARK Electronics, AVerMedia, Bosch, Emerson, Intrinsic, Kontron, L&amp;T Technology Services, Mistral, STIGA, Synopsys and Virya Autonomous Tech, among others. According to market research cited by the company, the global Physical AI devices market, including robotics, automotive and drones, is projected to reach 145 million cumulative shipments by 2035. SiMa.ai said Physical AI applications have traditionally relied on NVIDIA GPUs, which can be expensive and power intensive. The company offers a full-stack Physical AI platform that combines purpose-built silicon and software to simplify deployments. Slated for H1 2028, the next-generation hardware will include machine learning IP, chiplets and SoCs. The company plans to target medium to high-end drones, humanoid robotics, automotive advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and AI-powered cockpits. "

subject: Longevity startup Vytalyou
object: Rs 9 Cr in pre-Series A round
source_quote: "Doctor-led longevity and preventive healthcare startup Vytalyou has raised Rs 9 crore in a pre-Series A round from Chetan Jain of Pharma Dose and Ratan Jain of Venus Industries at a valuation of around Rs 33 crore. The proceeds will be used to expand its network of Incremental Lifestyle Clinics in Mumbai, Vytalyou said in a press release. Founded in 2025 by Chirantan Bose and Preetesh Bhandari, Vytalyou provides preventive healthcare and longevity-focused services, combining diagnostics with personalised health interventions and medically supervised care. The Mumbai-based startup offers services across pathology, radiology, cardio-respiratory assessments, body composition evaluation, genetic and cancer screening, gut microbiome evaluation, personalised IV therapies and regenerative interventions. It also offers non-invasive pain management technologies for chronic musculoskeletal conditions. Vytalyou uses an AI-based algorithm for its Predictive Longevity Evaluation, which assesses an individual&quot;s health profile, biological ageing and potential health risks. Doctors review the assessment and develop a medically supervised care plan based on the findings. The company said it has served close to 1,000 clients since opening its first centre, with around half coming through walk-ins and the rest through word-of-mouth referrals. It plans to expand to 10 locations across India in the coming years. Vytalyou operates in India&quot;s growing preventive healthcare and longevity segment, which has also seen startups such as Biopeak, Cent, Elevate Now and Decode Age raise capital. Biopeak raised $2.7 million in follow-on funding in January this year, while Cent, co-founded by Practo&quot;s Shashank ND, raised around $5 million for its AI-led early-detection platform covering cancer, cardiac, neurological and metabolic risks. Elevate Now raised Rs 18 crore in a seed round, while Decode Age raised Rs 14.48 crore in a pre-Series A round to expand its longevity research, biomarker discovery, multi-omics and microbiome capabilities. "

subject: Kanurra
object: raised $6.5 million from six venture capital firms
source_quote:
After its $6.5 million raise from six prominent venture capital firms, Kanurra's ambitions are broader than ever: it seeks to rewrite the rules of the PBM industry.
PBMs & The Health Cost Crisis
Pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) are infamous for making healthcare more expensive for Americans. PBMs are middlemen that manage prescription drug benefits for insurance companies, and traditionally, these PBMs have made money from hiking drug costs.
PBMs generate revenue from the spread. When a patient picks up a drug from a pharmacy, a PBM might only reimburse that pharmacy $20, then bill the patient's employer or insurance plan $100, and pocket the difference. A report from the Federal Trade Commission found that some specialty generic drugs dispensed by PBM-affiliated pharmacies were marked up by over 1,000%. Over time, this translates to higher premiums, lower coverage, and less accessible healthcare for Americans.
Kanurra's goal is to fix this problem.
A Flat Fee Alternative
Instead of siphoning revenue from American patients via the spread, Kanurra charges employers a flat administrative fee. Unlike traditional PBMs, Kanurra does not charge hidden, spread, or rebate-based fees, and passes drug costs through without adding a markup. The savings from this business model land in the pockets of American patients, as well as the employers that fund their employees' health plans. For an employer paying for its employees' GLP-1 costs, Kanurra could cut the cost of an Ozempic fill from $969 to $485, a difference that would scale to $58,080 a year for a 250-person group on Semaglutide alone.
A few PBMs also follow a pass-through model. But these PBMs are heavily focused on the higher end of the market, prioritizing enterprise partners over small and medium-sized businesses. Other than Kanurra, transparent PBMs will not partner with small level-funded groups at all, a member segment that comprises millions of Americans.
Kanurra's founder, Semih Gultekin, says he seeks to “eliminate confusion and increase the accessibility of prescription medications.” Kanurra will partner with self and level-funded employers, with a specialty in small and medium-sized businesses. As opposed to legacy PBMs, Kanurra prides itself on its auditability. Kanurra's AI-powered model will enable instant employer-side auditing of drug expenditures, which typically takes days or weeks with legacy PBMs.
